headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write and execute in shared VS Code files while PaddleOCR can ingest browser/file content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP/browsers; PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers. If PaddleOCR outputs are placed into shared files or browser-derived content, Roo Code may treat them as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible in default workspace use, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is written into a workspace file that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code parses OCR output or browser content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep OCR outputs in a separate, read-only folder
Add a provenance prefix to all PaddleOCR outputs
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text
Review any file before Roo Code acts on it
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code has broad filesystem access and can send context to configured model APIs; PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If sensitive documents are OCR'd into the shared workspace, Roo Code can read them and potentially transmit them onward. This is a default workspace risk, not a purely manual edge case.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or images are placed in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace context to a third-party model API
mitigations: Store sensitive inputs outside the shared workspace
Use a local-only model configuration for Roo Code
Redact secrets before OCR or coding steps
Restrict workspace permissions to least privilege
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on workspace reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write files, modify git state, and run shell commands in a workspace-scoped session; PaddleOCR can also operate on files and browser-derived content. Shared filesystem state plus concurrent modification creates a real conflict path, and the profile explicitly says Roo Code shares state via filesystem. Uncertainty about PaddleOCR write behavior does not reduce the risk enough, so choose higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Roo Code and PaddleOCR modify the same files or git state in overlapping sessions
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches for each agent
Add file-locking around shared outputs
requires-engineering: orchestrate mutual exclusion across sessions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and execute shell or git actions, while PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images. If Roo Code consumes OCR output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commands. The pair has a clear handoff path, but the blast radius is usually bounded to work products.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is fed directly into Roo Code prompts or tasks
IF Roo Code executes actions based on OCR text without human verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before actions
Compare OCR output against the source document
Limit Roo Code to draft-only mode for OCR-derived tasks
Mark OCR text as untrusted input
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR is open-source document processing with documents/images, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots plus model API keys. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible from the profiles. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of mixed data classes.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by PaddleOCR and then copied into Roo Code workspaces
IF Roo Code sends those materials to a non-compliant external model API
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use a compliant model endpoint
Separate retention policies by workspace
Document data handling boundaries
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end-to-end
